title: Dedicated: residency audit summarizer + selective retention hooks for tenant isolation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a Residency Audit Summarizer that compiles per-tenant isolation evidence (node assignment, region, network enclave, KMS key used) into a signed daily manifest, and add selective retention hooks so Dedicated tenants can opt retention windows for telemetry and artifacts. The feature should integrate with the existing attestation exporter, produce compact human- and machine-readable reports for auditors, and enable automated pruning/archival based on tenant policy. This ticket covers design, implementation of summarizer, retention hook API, storage rules (immutable/S3 object-lock), and tests / rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Daily signed manifest generated for each Dedicated tenant containing: tenant id, node identifiers, AZ/region map, snapshot hash of attestation artifacts, KMS key fingerprint, timestamp range.
Manifest is cryptographically signed with cluster signing key and verifiable via public endpoint; verification docs published.
Retention hooks API allows tenant admins to set retention windows for: logs (7/30/90/365 days), telemetry (30/90/365), attestation artifacts (immutable for configurable days).
Retention job enforces policy and moves eligible artifacts to archival S3 with object-lock when requested.
Automated tests that validate manifest contents, signature verification, and retention pruning in staging.
Migration path for existing attestation exports so customers with active Dedicated tenants get an initial baseline manifest.
Operational dashboards: per-tenant manifest generation success rate, retention-job failures, and storage reclaimed metrics are visible in Console.
design_decisions: Use append-only daily manifests (JSONL) stored in tenant-specific S3 prefixes; manifests include a SHA256 of the day's artifact bundle for tamper-evidence.
Sign manifests with an ed25519 cluster signing key managed via KMS; store public key in a read-only endpoint for auditor verification.
Leverage existing attestation-exporter pipeline (ENG-403210) as the source-of-truth for artifact lists; summarizer runs as a scheduled job immediately after export completes.
Implement retention rules as a declarative field on the tenant resource (redwood-dedicated API) and as a webhook to the cleanup worker for actioning.
For immutable retention (attestation artifacts), use S3 Object Lock + governance mode when tenant selects immutable retention; otherwise normal archival with lifecycle rules.
To reduce egress/cost, store compressed archive bundles (.tar.gz) and publish bundle hashes in the manifest rather than duplicating payloads in the manifest.
Fallback behavior: if the summarizer job fails for a tenant, emit a flagged manifest with failure reason and trigger an alert to oncall; do not alter retention settings.
implementation_steps: 1) Design schema for manifest (fields, versioning) and publish spec in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Residency+Audit+Manifest+Spec
2) Extend attestation-exporter to emit bundle metadata to summarizer topic (Kafka): PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/attestation-exporter/pull/266
3) Build summarizer service (go) that consumes topic, composes manifest, signs with cluster KMS key, writes to tenant S3 prefix, and emits telemetry to Console.
4) Add tenant API fields for retention preferences; UI stub in Console to set defaults (PM separate ticket).
5) Implement retention-hook worker to reconcile tenant policy and schedule archival/prune jobs.
6) Add S3 lifecycle + Object Lock provisioning for new tenant buckets; infra automation in Terraform modules.
7) Create CLI/README for auditors: verification steps + sample commands to fetch and verify manifests.
8) End-to-end tests in staging that simulate retention transitions and verify manifest signatures and artifact immutability.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge summarizer behind a feature-flag; enable for internal test tenants only.
Week 1: Smoke tests + oncall runbook rehearsal; generate manifests for 5 pilot tenants.
Week 2: Open beta for invited customers; monitor Console metrics and storage impact.
Week 3: Gradual ramp to all new Dedicated tenants; offer migration tool for existing tenants to generate baseline manifests.
Full enablement contingent on security-review signoff and SRE checklist completion.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest composer and signer (coverage > 90%).
Integration tests: summarizer + attestation-exporter + S3 writes in staging cluster.
Property tests for retention-hook worker to ensure no under/over deletion for boundary windows.
Chaos test: randomly kill summarizer job to ensure observed failure manifest and alerting works.
Manual audit: run verification steps from auditor README against staging manifests.
